title: 9 Dead After Far-Right Gunman Opens Fire in Krakow Plaza and Murders Family
snippet: A 25-year-old suspect opened fire in a crowded medieval square in Krakow, Poland, killing six bystanders before police discovered his parents and sister dead at his home.
content:
KRAKOW, Poland — A deadly terror attack rocked one of Europe's most famous historic districts Saturday when a gunman clad in tactical gear opened fire in Krakow's packed Main Market Square, killing six people and wounding 16 others. The horror deepened hours later when police searching the suspect's home discovered three more bodies—his father, mother, and sister—bringing the total death toll to nine.

Polish authorities have launched a formal counterterrorism investigation into the 25-year-old suspect, who officers shot and took into custody within three minutes of the first emergency calls. Officials said preliminary evidence points to far-right, ultra-nationalist extremism as the primary motive behind the massacre.

Three Minutes of Terror

The attack unfolded shortly before 3:00 p.m. local time in the heart of Krakow’s bustling tourist center. Witnesses described scenes of utter panic as the assailant drove into the medieval plaza and began firing indiscriminately at pedestrians from inside his vehicle. Gunfire shattered windows on a passing tram, though no passengers aboard were hit.

Armed officers rushed to the scene and engaged the shooter in an intense gunfight. Two officers, identified by Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk as Senior Constables Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, sustained gunshot wounds during the confrontation. One officer was reported in critical condition after being shot three times while subduing the attacker. The suspect remains hospitalized in stable condition following emergency surgery for abdominal and chest wounds.

Dark Discovery at Suspect's Home

As bomb squads swept the shooter's vehicle for explosives near the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, counterterrorism units raided his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, roughly 125 miles northeast of Krakow. Inside, investigators discovered the bodies of the suspect’s 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother, and 21-year-old sister.

Police confirmed the shooter held a valid firearms permit and was carrying military-grade weaponry alongside extensive stockpiles of ammunition. Despite wearing military attire, officials clarified he was not a member of the armed forces.

Global Outcry and Local Mourning

The six plaza victims included four women and two men. Polish authorities confirmed one British national was among the dead, alongside three Polish citizens, while two victims remain unidentified. The 16 injured included tourists from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal, and Russia.

"Until now, in Poland, we haven't seen such drastic cases of terrorism," Prime Minister Tusk said after arriving in Krakow. "That is what we must call this cruel attack on human life."

Krakow Mayor Łukasz Gibała declared an official citywide period of mourning through November 11. World leaders, including U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, expressed outrage and solidarity with the victims, with Rose condemning the violence as a "savage and murderous attack."
